headline: Malaysia to hire 200,000 Bangladeshi workers in six months, 10,000 free of cost
summary: Malaysia plans to recruit 200,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next six months, with 10,000 positions offered free of charge. This move comes alongside discussions of a $2 billion investment in Bangladesh's EV, solar, renewable energy, and halal food secto
details: Malaysia is set to recruit approximately 200,000 workers from Bangladesh within the next six months. A significant aspect of this recruitment drive is that 10,000 of these workers will be hired free of cost.

The recruitment process will be facilitated through various agencies in Bangladesh, with phases expected to commence from the end of September. This timeline aims for completion within the specified six-month period.

The announcement followed a meeting between Malaysian High Commissioner Mohd Shuhada Othman and LGRD Minister Abdul Moyeen Khan at the Secretariat. State Minister Mir Shahe Alam shared these details with reporters.

During the discussions, preparations were also noted for a substantial US $2 billion investment by Malaysia in Bangladesh. This investment targets key sectors including electric vehicles, solar panels, renewable energy, and halal food.

The meeting also touched upon strengthening friendly relations between the two nations and a potential visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Malaysia. The issue of unregistered Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia was raised, with a request for their registration.

Currently, about 800,000 Bangladeshi workers are officially registered in Malaysia. The new recruitment and investment initiatives are expected to further bolster economic ties and provide significant employment opportunities.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh to buy billion-dollar Boeing aircraft]], US envoy calls deal 'extraordinary'
headline: Bangladesh to buy billion-dollar Boeing aircraft, US envoy calls deal 'extraordinary'
summary: Bangladesh has committed to a multi-billion dollar agreement to purchase Boeing aircraft, a move praised by US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gore as an 'extraordinary deal'.
details: Bangladesh has agreed to purchase billion-dollar Boeing aircraft, a deal welcomed by US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gore. He described the new agreement, made between US President Donald Trump and Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tareque Rahman, as 'extraordinary'.
Gore shared his remarks on Sunday, August 30, via a post on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). In his message, the top US diplomat lauded the Trump administration's efforts.
He stated, 'This week, another extraordinary agreement was reached between President Trump and the Prime Minister of Bangladesh. Under this, Bangladesh has pledged to spend billions of dollars'.

Highlighting Trump's contributions to the US economy, Sergio Gore asserted that Donald Trump is the greatest president in US history for job creation. He added that Trump is tirelessly working to create higher-paying jobs, attract trillions of dollars in investment, and boost the economy.
Earlier, US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gore, visited Dhaka for a three-day trip on July 30. His recent comments underscore the growing economic ties between the two nations.
caption:
Bangladesh is set to acquire billion-dollar Boeing aircraft following an agreement between President Trump and PM Tareque Rahman. US Special Envoy Sergio Gore has hailed it as an 'extraordinary deal'.

Bangladesh has agreed to purchase billion-dollar Boeing aircraft, a deal welcomed by US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gore. He described the new agreement, made between US President Donald Trump and Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tareque Rahman, as 'extraordinary'.

Gore shared his remarks on Sunday, August 30, via a post on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). In his message, the top US diplomat lauded the Trump administration's efforts.

He stated, 'This week, another extraordinary agreement was reached between President Trump and the Prime Minister of Bangladesh. Under this, Bangladesh has pledged to spend billions of dollars'.

Highlighting Trump's contributions to the US economy, Sergio Gore asserted that Donald Trump is the greatest president in US history for job creation. He added that Trump is tirelessly working to create higher-paying jobs, attract trillions of dollars in investment, and boost the economy.

Earlier, US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gore, visited Dhaka for a three-day trip on July 30. His recent comments underscore the growing economic ties between the two nations.
